title: Constructible subobjects on a Noetherian vanishing topos
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact), $f:X\to S$ a morphism of finite presentation, and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring. Use the vanishing topos $V_f$ and its category of sheaves of modules over the constant ring $\Lambda$ from [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles], and finite-stratification constructibility from [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf]. Every subsheaf and every quotient sheaf of a constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf on $V_f$ is constructible. In an exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ of such sheaves, if $A$ and $C$ are constructible, then $B$ is constructible. Consequently kernels, cokernels, images and finite extensions of constructible sheaves on $V_f$ are constructible.

source.place: Section 8.1 and Lemma 8.3.3, printed p. 19 (author draft).

proof.text: First establish the ambient finiteness needed below. Finite presentation implies finite type (a finite algebra presentation supplies finite generators), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. Both $X$ and $S$ are quasi-compact and, by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], quasi-separated; $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by its finite-presentation hypothesis. Apply [lem-trf-qcqs-oriented-triple-presentation] to $X\to S\leftarrow S$, and then [lem-trf-finitary-site-coherent-generators] and [lem-trf-finitary-site-enough-points]. Thus $V_f$ is coherent and its points jointly detect isomorphisms. These statements apply equally to the finite-presentation maps over closed subschemes of $S$ occurring below.

source.place: Section 8.1 and the opening of 8.2, printed pp. 17–18; the finite-cover site gives coherence and enough points.

proof.text: We prove an auxiliary ascending-chain assertion for finite-set sheaves. For closed subschemes $Z\subseteq X$, $T\subseteq S$ with their reduced structures put $E_{Z,T}=Z_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}T_{\mathrm{Et}}$. Say that a sheaf of sets on this topos is constructible when finite constructible locally closed partitions of $Z,T$ make it locally constant finite on each rectangular oriented product. The claim is that every increasing sequence $A_0\subseteq A_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F$ of constructible set sheaves with constructible $F$ stabilizes. Induct on the pair of closed subsets $(Z,T)$, ordered by inclusion in both coordinates with at least one strict inclusion. This is well founded by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]: first minimize one coordinate of any nonempty family of pairs, then the other among that coordinate's fibre. If either coordinate is empty the topos has only its empty point support and all its sheaves are isomorphic, so the claim holds. By [lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-restriction], $E_{Z,T}\simeq V_{Z_T/T}$, preserving precisely this constructibility. Closed immersions have affine presentations $R\to R/I$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]; over a Noetherian affine every $I$ has finite generators by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], so they are of finite presentation. Thus $T,Z,Z_T$ are Noetherian by the finite-type argument of Step 1. Base change preserves finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]; composition with the closed immersion $Z_T\to X_T$ preserves it by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](d). Hence Step 1 and [lem-trf-oriented-maximal-point-finiteness] apply to this topos. Assume the ascending-chain assertion for all strictly smaller closed pairs.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 8.3.3, first paragraph, printed p. 19: Noetherian induction on the two closed coordinates; Lemma 8.3.1 identifies the closed-base pieces.

proof.text: First choose dense opens $U_0\subseteq Z$, $V_0\subseteq T$ on whose rectangle $E'_0=U_{0,\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}V_{0,\mathrm{Et}}$ the sheaf $F$ is locally constant with finite values. There are finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. For a generic point $\eta$ of $Z$, the stratum of the witnessing finite partition containing $\eta$ is $O\cap C$ with $O$ open and $C\supseteq\overline{\{\eta\}}$ closed, so $W_\eta=O$ minus the other components is an open neighbourhood of $\eta$ inside that stratum; the $W_\eta$ are disjoint and their union $U_0$ is dense. Do the same in $T$. By [lem-trf-oriented-maximal-point-finiteness] there are finitely many maximal point classes of $E_{Z,T}$; let $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ be those lying in $E'_0$, i.e. at which the subterminal of $E'_0$ has nonempty stalk. Each $F_{p_i}$ is finite: some member $U_k$ of a trivializing covering has an element at $p_i$, and on $E'_0/U_k$ the sheaf $F$ is constant on a finite set, whose stalk is that set. The $(A_n)_{p_i}$ increase inside $F_{p_i}$, so choose $N$ with $(A_n)_{p_i}=(A_N)_{p_i}$ for all $i$ and $n\geq N$. Then apply the same construction to $F$ and $A_N$ together, taking each $W_\eta$ inside the strata of both partitions and inside $U_0$ (resp. $V_0$): this gives dense opens $U\subseteq U_0$, $V\subseteq V_0$ on whose rectangle $E'=U_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}V_{\mathrm{Et}}$ both $A_N$ and $F$ are locally constant with finite values. The rectangles are open subtopoi of $E_{Z,T}$: by the projection formulas of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] the subterminal $p_1^{-1}U\times p_2^{-1}V$ is the sheaf associated with the triple $(U\to S\leftarrow V)$, and by [lem-trf-oriented-slice-localization] the slice over it is $U_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}V_{\mathrm{Et}}$; likewise for $E'_0$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 8.3.3, first paragraph, printed p. 19: uniform index at maximal points and generic rectangular local constancy.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq N$ and a point $p$ of $E'$. Choose a maximal generization $q$ of $p$ using [lem-trf-oriented-maximal-point-finiteness]. It lies in $E'$: the transformation $p^{-1}\Rightarrow q^{-1}$ carries the unique element of the open subterminal at $p$ to an element at $q$. Since $E'\subseteq E'_0$, the class of $q$ is one of $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ of Step 3. On a locally constant sheaf this transformation is a bijection on stalks. Indeed, choose a trivializing covering object with an element at $p$; its image supplies a lift at $q$, and on this slice the transformation on a constant set is the identity. Apply this to $A_N$ and $F$. Naturality identifies the inclusion $(A_N)_p\subseteq F_p$ with $(A_N)_q\subseteq F_q$. Any element of $(A_n)_p$ maps into $(A_n)_q=(A_N)_q$, so its image in $F_p$ belongs to $(A_N)_p$. Thus $(A_n)_p=(A_N)_p$. The points are conservative by Step 1 (also on an open subtopos, whose points are just the points where its subterminal is inhabited), so $A_n=A_N$ on $E'$. This argument does not assume that all the $A_n$ are locally constant on one common open, nor that the maximal points excluded by $E'$ remain in it.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 8.3.3, first paragraph, printed p. 19: why generic equality forces equality on the chosen open rectangle.

proof.text: The remaining points of $E_{Z,T}$ lie on $E_{Z\setminus U,T}$ or $E_{Z,T\setminus V}$. For the first piece this is the closed complement assertion of [lem-trf-oriented-source-localization] after the identification with $V_{Z_T/T}$; for the second it is [lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-restriction]. Restricting a finite-stratification constructible set sheaf to either piece preserves constructibility: intersect its witnessing strata with the closed subsets, and pull back its local constant trivializations. Both pairs are strictly smaller, so the induction hypothesis supplies stabilization indices on these two pieces. The maximum of these indices and $N$ gives equality on every point of the whole topos, hence equality by Step 1. This closes the induction and proves the ascending-chain assertion at $(X,S)$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 8.3.3, first paragraph, printed p. 19: closing the two-coordinate Noetherian induction on the complement of the open rectangle.

proof.text: Let $G\subseteq F$ now be any subsheaf of sets, where $F$ is constructible. By [lem-trf-coherent-set-criterion], $F$ is coherent. Step 1 and [lem-trf-coherent-object-approximation] give $G\simeq\operatorname{colim}_i C_i$ with coherent $C_i$. The images $B_i=\operatorname{im}(C_i\to G\to F)$ are coherent, and so constructible by the same criterion. They form a directed family of subobjects with union $G$: every local section of the colimit comes locally from some $C_i$, and a common target for any two indices contains both images. If this family had no maximal member, recursively choosing a strictly larger member would give a nonstationary increasing sequence of constructible subsheaves of $F$, contrary to Step 5. A maximal member $B$ contains every $B_i$, because directedness gives a member containing both and maximality makes it equal to $B$. Thus $G=B$ is constructible. All diagrams and subobject families are small in [def-weil-size-convention]; this argument is about set-valued images, not images of an unspecified module approximation.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 8.3.3, second paragraph, printed p. 19, using the filtered coherent approximation of Section 8.1.

proof.text: For a constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf $B$ and any module subsheaf $A\subseteq B$, [lem-trf-oriented-constructible-coherent] makes $|B|$ coherent, hence constructible as a set sheaf by [lem-trf-coherent-set-criterion]. The underlying map $|A|\to|B|$ is a monomorphism of set sheaves. Step 6 makes $|A|$ constructible, so the set criterion makes it coherent, and the converse direction of [lem-trf-oriented-constructible-coherent] makes $A$ constructible as a module sheaf. The finite coefficient ring is unchanged throughout. This proves the arbitrary-subobject clause without replacing module constructibility by an unproved set-valued identification.

source.place: Lemma 8.3.3(1), finite-module variant using Section 8.1; set-to-module constructibility is the existing coherent criterion.

proof.text: On any rectangular stratum, [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-derived-serre] applies to its small defining site and to $\Lambda$. This ring is Noetherian since each ideal is a finite set and is generated by that finite list, as required by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; a finite $\Lambda$-module is finitely generated, and a finitely generated module over finite $\Lambda$ is a quotient of a finite set $\Lambda^d$, hence finite. Thus the cited theorem gives finite locally constant kernels, cokernels and extensions on the stratum. Inverse image along its geometric morphism preserves exact sequences of constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves: it preserves finite limits and, being a left adjoint, colimits, with $u^{-1}\Lambda=\Lambda$. For two constructible sheaves take the finite common refinements of their partitions of $X$ and of $S$, formed by intersections of locally closed strata; their pullbacks preserve the constant trivializations. Applying the cited theorem on every refined rectangle proves closure under kernels and cokernels of morphisms between constructible sheaves, and constructibility of the middle term of an extension whose outer terms are constructible.

source.place: Section 8.1 and the closure under kernels, cokernels and extensions used in the proof of Proposition 9.1.2, printed p. 20; the local exact-sequence input is the existing theorem for every small site.

proof.text: For an arbitrary quotient $B\twoheadrightarrow C$ with $B$ constructible, its kernel $A\subseteq B$ is constructible by Step 7. Apply Step 8 to the morphism $A\to B$ between constructible sheaves: its cokernel is $C$, so $C$ is constructible. Images are subobjects of their constructible target (Step 7), or cokernels of constructible kernels (Step 8). Iterating the extension clause handles every finite extension. These give all clauses of the statement.

source.place: Lemma 8.3.3 and the exact-sequence closure used in Proposition 9.1.2; final elementary abelian-category deduction.
